summary: 48-foot steel lookout tower erected on Almanac Mountain, Lakeville Plantation, Maine in 1921; cab removed 2009; steel tower listed standing, condition unconfirmed.

facts.status_note: Steel tower still listed as standing; the cab was removed in 2009 (Forest Lookouts), and we found no later confirmation of its condition

events.note: New lookout station established on Almanac Mountain in Lakeville Plantation, with glasses, maps and a half-mile telephone line (1914 Forest Commissioner's report, quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Newspaper report of April 28, 1921 says a five-man crew was erecting a 48-foot steel lookout tower on Almanac Mountain
The observer's camp at the site was burned in the fall; the source does not say how or whether the tower was affected
Maine chapter report: tower deteriorated and badly vandalized; Maine Forest Service wanted to remove it for safety reasons; listed for possible removal in 2009
Tower cab removed, leaving the steel tower on the site

notes_for_editor: Dates: Forest Lookouts dates a lookout station to 1914 and the tower erection to April 1921; we record 1921 for the tower. Two web search summaries say the first tower was 1914 and moved to Dill Ridge in 1927 and back, a 1998 preservation effort, a 1967 reinstallation and a 2021 condition note; none of those pages could be read (the Hilton legacy page returned 404, towerdex returned 403, and a Maine archives link returned 404), so none is in the story or the JSON. Check firelookout.org's Maine record and the Maine Forest Service before publishing a current condition. The 2008 report's 'may be removed in 2009' is a plan, not proof of removal. Brief lacked a build date; agency kept as the brief's Maine Forestry District from the Forest Lookouts header, while the 2008 report names the Maine Forest Service. Access unknown. No photos added.
